*World Obesity Day: Obesity & Obstructive Sleep Apnea – A Silent Connection*

Obesity is more than a number on the weighing scale — it significantly impacts breathing during sleep. One of the most serious yet under-diagnosed consequences is Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA).

Excess body weight, especially around the neck and upper airway, narrows the breathing passage. During sleep, these tissues collapse more easily, causing repeated pauses in breathing. This leads to loud snoring, choking episodes at night, poor-quality sleep, and excessive daytime fatigue.

Studies show that obesity is the strongest risk factor for OSA. A higher Body Mass Index (BMI) and increased neck circumference markedly increase the risk. Untreated OSA can contribute to hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, reduced concentration, mood changes, and even increased surgical risks.

The encouraging news? Even a 5–10% reduction in body weight can significantly improve sleep apnea severity. Weight loss, lifestyle modification, CPAP therapy, and in select cases, surgical intervention can dramatically improve quality of life.
If you experience loud snoring, daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, or unrefreshing sleep — don’t ignore it.
